label: assertion
text: The trajectory of out-of-distribution (OOD) detection performance, measured by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and related metrics, during supervised training decomposes into three distinct stages: (A) an initial stage where training and test error fall and AUROC improves; (B) a subsequent overfitting stage where the training error approaches zero and test error can continue to decrease while AUROC decreases; and (C) a final instability stage where classification test error is stable but AUROC varies sharply across nearby checkpoints, making final-checkpoint selection unreliable.

label: assertion
text: The instability of out-of-distribution (OOD) metrics near the final checkpoint arises from the trained solution being fragile to small perturbations of network weights.

label: 论据
text: Evaluating the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and the false positive rate at 95% true positive rate (FPR95) as the weights are moved along random normalized directions \(d\) with small scalar magnitude \(\alpha\) (i.e., \(\theta(d,\alpha)=\theta_{\text{final}}+\alpha\cdot d\)) shows narrow optima in the weight space causing sharp metric changes for small \(\alpha\).

label: assertion
text: Applying exponential moving-weight averaging (Model Averaging, MA) stabilizes OOD performance by producing a smoother / wider optimum.

label: 论据
text: The averaged parameters \(\theta^{\mathrm{MA}}\), implemented as the exponential moving average of parameters after an epoch \(t_0\) (\(\theta_{t+1}^{\mathrm{MA}}=\theta_t\) for \(t<t_0\), and \(\theta_{t+1}^{\mathrm{MA}}=\tau\cdot \theta_t^{\mathrm{MA}} + (1-\tau)\cdot \theta_{t+1}\) for \(t\ge t_0\), with \(\tau=\dfrac{t-t_0}{t-t_0+1}\)), yield substantially reduced AUROC and FPR95 sensitivity to small weight perturbations and smoother AUROC curves during training across scoring functions.

label: assertion
text: For a simplified linear-Gaussian model that isolates a special discriminative feature and \(d\) abundant weak common features, the Bayes classifier and its in-distribution (ID) classification risk and out-of-distribution (OOD) detection (rejection) risk admit closed-form expressions.

label: 论据
text: The Bayes logit is \[ f_{\mathrm{Bayes}}(\boldsymbol{x}) = x_1 + \eta\sum_{i=2}^{d+1} x_i, \] and the resulting risks simplify to \[ \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{ID}}(f_{\mathrm{Bayes}})=\Pr\!\left\{\mathcal{N}(0,1)>\frac{\sqrt{1+d\eta^2}}{\sigma}\right\}, \] \[ \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{OOD}}(f_{\mathrm{Bayes}})=\Pr\!\left\{\mathcal{N}(0,1)>\frac{\delta-d\eta^2}{\sigma\sqrt{1+d\eta^2}}\right\}+\Pr\!\left\{\mathcal{N}(0,1)>\frac{\delta+d\eta^2}{\sigma\sqrt{1+d\eta^2}}\right\}, \] where \(\delta\) is the rejection threshold.

label: assertion
text: These formulas show that increasing the number \(d\) of common weak features (with \(0<\eta\ll1\) and \(d\gg1\)) can markedly increase OOD risk.

label: assertion
text: These formulas show that increasing the number \(d\) of common weak features (with \(0<\eta\ll1\) and \(d\gg1\)) only slowly improves ID classification.

label: 论据
text: Solving the squared-error empirical risk with least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regularization parameter \(\lambda\), \[ \min_{\boldsymbol{w}}\ \mathbb{E}_{(x,y)\sim\mathcal{D}_\text{ID}}\!\left\{\tfrac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\boldsymbol{w}^\top\boldsymbol{x}}{\sigma}-y\right)^2+\lambda\|\boldsymbol{w}\|_1\right\}, \] yields the closed-form trimmed coefficient vector \[ f_{\text{LASSO}}(\boldsymbol{x}) = (1-\lambda)_+\,x_1 + \sum_{i=2}^{d+1} (\eta-\lambda)_+\, x_i, \] where \((\cdot)_+\) denotes the positive part.

label: assertion
text: This analytic solution demonstrates that an \(L_1\) penalty can suppress coefficients on abundant weak common features (feature selection) (by choosing \(\lambda\approx\eta\)).

label: assertion
text: As a consequence of 【16】, this thereby reduces OOD detection risk at controlled cost to ID accuracy.

text: The combined module, Average of Pruning (AoP), which combines iterative magnitude pruning with parameter averaging, is applied without modifying existing scoring functions.

label: assertion
text: Applying Average of Pruning (AoP) as a plug-in improves out-of-distribution (OOD) detection performance across multiple benchmarks and scoring methods.

label: example
text: On ResNet-18 trained on CIFAR-10, applying AoP to K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) increases average area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) across six OOD datasets from 94.39% to 95.04% and reduces average false positive rate at 95% true positive rate (FPR95) from 34.42% to 25.30%.

label: example
text: Applying AoP to Virtual-Logit Matching (ViM) on ResNet-18 trained on CIFAR-10 increases average AUROC from 94.18% to 95.69% and reduces average false positive rate at 95% true positive rate (FPR95) from 32.27% to 25.3%.

label: assertion
text: AoP also improves multiple scoring functions.

label: assertion
text: AoP scales to larger datasets.

label: example
text: On Tiny-ImageNet, AoP improves MSP AUROC by 1.5–3.3 percentage points on Textures, LSUN, and iSUN.

label: example
text: On ImageNet, AoP yields AUROC improvements of 0.3–0.7 percentage points across scoring functions on Places, SUN, and Textures.

label: assertion
text: The improvements in out-of-distribution (OOD) detection performance achieved by applying Average of Pruning (AoP) as a plug-in hold across backbones.

label: assertion
text: The improvements in out-of-distribution (OOD) detection performance achieved by applying Average of Pruning (AoP) as a plug-in remain when combining AoP with Outlier Exposure (OE).

text: Iterative magnitude pruning (Lottery Ticket Hypothesis (LTH) style with weight rewinding) reduces the late-stage overfitting of out-of-distribution (OOD) detection.

label: assertion
text: As global sparsity is increased from dense toward moderate sparsity, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) on out-of-distribution (OOD) tasks first increases and then eventually decreases if pruning becomes too aggressive and removes discriminative capacity.

label: assertion
text: Visualization of final-layer features shows that pruned models produce larger ID-versus-OOD feature differences than dense models.

label: 论据
text: Among during-training pruning methods evaluated, iterative/post-training LTH performed best for OOD tasks in CIFAR-10 experiments with ResNet-18.

text: Ablation experiments establish that both components—model averaging (MA) and pruning—are required.

label: example
text: On CIFAR-10 with ResNet-18: baseline AUROC = 91.63%; with pruning alone AUROC increases to 92.94%; with pruning plus MA (AoP) AUROC further increases to 93.32%.

label: assertion

label: assertion
text: Average of Pruning (AoP) not only improves out-of-distribution (OOD) detection but also enhances misclassification detection (detecting when the classifier will be wrong on in-distribution inputs).

label: 论据
text: On WideResNet-40-2 trained on CIFAR-10, applying AoP to Maximum Softmax Probability (MSP) improves the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) for misclassification detection from 92.51% to 93.23%, reduces the area under the risk-coverage curve (AURC) from \(7.55\times 10^{-3}\) to \(6.41\times 10^{-3}\), and reduces the false positive rate at 95% true positive rate (FPR95) from 40.87% to 38.47%.

label: assertion
text: Similar improvements to those described in 【1, 3】 are observed when AoP is combined with other confidence estimators.
